title: Vaping and Cancer: The Evidence Is Mounting
hook: A major review concludes nicotine vapes are likely to cause lung and oral cancers — challenging the idea that vaping is a harmless alternative to smoking.
key_points: A major evidence review concludes nicotine vapes are likely to cause lung and oral cancers.
The conclusion draws on human biomarker data plus animal and laboratory studies.
It challenges the common belief that vaping is a harmless alternative to cigarettes.
Cancer risks may emerge sooner than many had assumed.
content_html: Vaping has often been sold as the safer cousin of cigarettes. A major evidence review summarized by ScienceDaily complicates that story: the researchers conclude that nicotine vapes are likely to cause lung and oral cancers.
extra_html:
The conclusion doesn't rest on one study. The reviewers weighed evidence across several types — biomarkers measured in people who vape, plus animal and laboratory studies — and found the pattern consistent enough to judge the cancer risk likely rather than merely theoretical. They also note that some harms may show up sooner than many had assumed.

A few caveats worth holding in mind: "likely to cause" is a careful scientific phrase, not proof of a specific personal risk, and vaping is still generally considered less harmful than continuing to smoke combustible cigarettes. But the review pushes back hard on the idea that vaping is harmless — especially for people who never smoked and took up vaping believing it carried no real risk. For anyone using vapes to quit smoking, the goal remains getting off nicotine entirely rather than switching to a habit that may carry its own long-term dangers.
